title: France’s Catholic Revival Is Fueling Its Far Right
gist: Pope Leo XIV's mass-attended Paris visit drew nearly every 2027 French presidential contender, including the National Rally's Marine Le Pen and Jordan Bardella, reflecting a sharp rise in Catholic support for the far right (20% to 36% between 2012 and 2022 per Ifop). Robert Zaretsky cautions that the far-right Catholic vote is strongest among non-practicing Catholics, and that the touted religious revival may be as fleeting as the one after John Paul II's 1997 visit amid long-run de-Christianization.

themes.theme: Catholic vote shifting to the RN

insights.claim: According to an Ifop survey, the share of French Catholics voting for Marine Le Pen and her party nearly doubled from 20 percent to 36 percent between the 2012 and 2022 presidential elections.
insights.speaker: Robert Zaretsky
insights.so_what: Broadening of the far-right electoral base raises the probability of a National Rally presidency in France's spring election, a key risk for French assets and EU cohesion.
insights.quote: the percentage of Catholics who cast their votes for Le Pen and her party nearly doubled, from 20 percent to 36 percent.

insights.claim: French Catholics' drift toward the far right accelerated as Pope Francis openly sided with the homeless and stateless and criticized populist parties' Islamophobic and xenophobic positions.
insights.speaker: Robert Zaretsky
insights.so_what: Voter migration responds to identity and immigration issues more than church guidance, limiting institutional brakes on populism.

insights.claim: Marine Le Pen and Jordan Bardella attended Pope Leo XIV's Paris welcome, an institutional Catholic event party founder Jean-Marie Le Pen would never have attended, signaling the RN's courtship of Catholic voters ahead of her fourth presidential bid.
insights.speaker: Robert Zaretsky
insights.so_what: Indicates the RN's continuing normalization strategy to widen its coalition before a decisive election.

insights.claim: Economic status shapes French Catholic voting: well-to-do Catholics still lean center or left, while working-class Catholics increasingly lean to the extreme right.
insights.speaker: Robert Zaretsky
insights.so_what: Class rather than faith is the stronger driver of far-right support, linking RN momentum to cost-of-living pressures.

insights.claim: In the 2024 European elections, 41 percent of French self-identified Catholics who never attend church voted for the RN, versus only 18 percent of weekly Mass-goers.
insights.speaker: Robert Zaretsky
insights.so_what: The 'Catholic revival fuels the far right' story is mostly about cultural, not practicing, Catholics, suggesting identity politics rather than religiosity drives the vote.

insights.claim: Practicing Catholics are a much smaller French voting bloc than at the Fifth Republic's birth (about 33 percent in 1958), but the Catholic vote can still be decisive in a close election; about 10 million French identify as practicing Catholics.
insights.speaker: Robert Zaretsky
insights.so_what: A swing bloc worth watching in polling for France's next presidential election.

insights.claim: After taking over in 2011, Marine Le Pen renamed the National Front the National Rally, purged neo-Nazi and antisemitic elements, and aligned with some liberal policies such as legalized abortion and euthanasia, which drove most Catholic traditionalists out of the party.
insights.speaker: Robert Zaretsky
insights.so_what: The RN's de-demonization is central to its mainstream electability and thus to French political-risk pricing.

insights.claim: Marine Le Pen has pledged that one of her first acts as president would be applying 'national priority' to give French citizens privileged access to government-controlled housing, a rule the author describes as unconstitutional and, per housing experts, impractical.
insights.speaker: Robert Zaretsky
insights.so_what: Signals likely early constitutional clashes and policy friction under an RN presidency.

insights.claim: French Muslims remain overwhelmingly opposed to the National Rally regardless of economic status.
insights.speaker: Robert Zaretsky
insights.so_what: Polarization along religious lines raises social-cohesion risk under a far-right government.

insights.claim: France's Society of Saint Pius X integralist movement numbers about 30,000 members across more than 150 churches, and its school history manuals tend to glorify Vichy leader Philippe Pétain while omitting the Shoah.
insights.speaker: Robert Zaretsky
insights.so_what: Traditionalist Catholicism is a small but ideologically hard-right niche distinct from the RN's current mainstream base.

insights.claim: Pope Leo XIV's Paris visit drew about 800,000 spectators along the Champs-Elysées and nearly 80,000 youths to a Stade de France prayer vigil.
insights.speaker: Robert Zaretsky
insights.so_what: Large turnout fuels the narrative of a youth religious revival that could reshape French cultural politics.
insights.locator: The idea of a revival of religiosity

insights.claim: The idea of a religious revival among young French people is a popular meme but difficult to substantiate, and similar expectations after Pope John Paul II's 1997 Paris visit never materialized.
insights.speaker: Robert Zaretsky
insights.so_what: Caution against extrapolating event-driven religiosity into durable political realignment.
insights.quote: The idea of a revival of religiosity among young French people has become a well-traveled meme in the nation’s discourse, though it’s difficult to substantiate.
insights.locator: The idea of a revival of religiosity

insights.claim: Over the past three decades France's de-Christianization quickened, with priests falling from roughly 25,000 to 11,000 and annual church marriages collapsing from around 124,000 to 40,000.
insights.speaker: Robert Zaretsky
insights.so_what: Long-run secular decline undercuts claims that religiosity, rather than identity, drives far-right gains.
insights.quote: the ranks of priests tumbling from roughly 25,000 to 11,000 and the annual number of church marriages collapsing from around 124,000 to 40,000.

insights.claim: Only 2.4 million viewers watched the televised papal vigil at the Stade de France, while nearly 7 million watched a French men's national soccer team match instead.
insights.speaker: Robert Zaretsky
insights.so_what: A telling gauge that mass enthusiasm for the papal visit is narrower than headlines suggest.
insights.quote: while 2.4 million viewers watched the televised vigil at the Stade de France, nearly 7 million instead watched a match played by the French men’s soccer team.

insights.claim: France's Catholic bishops have been less vocal than German counterparts such as Gerhard Feige in warning against the rise of the extreme right, though the church has repeatedly called for humane treatment of migrants.
insights.speaker: Robert Zaretsky
insights.so_what: Weak institutional church opposition removes one potential brake on far-right normalization in France.
